subject: Your Friday 5: dog things for this weekend · The OC Pack
headline: 5 dog things to do in Orange County this weekend.
intro: Dachshund races in Placentia, Santa photos in Anaheim and Brea, and two good walks to work off Thanksgiving. Here is the weekend:

picks.name: Wienersgiving at The Bruery, Placentia
picks.detail: Sunday, 1 to 5 PM at The Bruery, 717 Dunn Way. This Thanksgiving themed dachshund meetup has races at 2 PM and a costume contest at 3 PM, plus pet vendors. Race sign up is 1 to 1:45 PM and the racer fee is $10 cash. Spectators and other breeds are welcome.

picks.name: Puppy Pics with Santa, Anaheim
picks.detail: Sunday, 2 to 4 PM at Colony Wine Merchant, 280 South Lemon Street. Bring your pup for a holiday photo with Santa to kick off the Christmas season, with photography by Parker's Pet Photos. Tickets are sold through the Colony Wine Merchant website, so check there before you go.

picks.name: Pet Photos with Santa, Brea Mall
picks.detail: Sunday, 6:30 to 8 PM in Center Court at Brea Mall, 1065 Brea Mall. Bring your pet to pose with Santa at this special pet photo session, with no reservation needed. The Santa set is near Sephora. Check the Brea Mall site before you go to confirm the session.

picks.name: Costa Mesa Bark Park
picks.detail: Friday through Sunday, 7:30 AM to 8:45 PM at 890 Arlington Drive, inside TeWinkle Park. Two fenced acres of off-leash play, with a separate area for small, elderly and disabled dogs, plus water, benches and free parking. The park is closed Wednesdays for maintenance.

picks.name: Upper Newport Bay Back Bay Loop, Newport Beach
picks.detail: Open 7 AM to sunset, starting at the Peter and Mary Muth Interpretive Center, 2301 University Drive. Walk the paved bay trails with your dog on a leash and watch for herons and egrets over the marsh. Parking is free at the center lot. Bring water for you and your dog.

trailGuide.name: Santiago Creek Trail, Santiago Oaks Regional Park, Orange
trailGuide.parking: Main lot at 2145 North Windes Drive, $5 per vehicle on weekends; park open 7 AM to sunset
trailGuide.shade: Good shade along the creek under the oaks, with sunnier stretches if you climb toward the ridge trails
trailGuide.leash: Required at all times, six foot maximum
trailGuide.note: The easy Santiago Creek Trail is just under a mile along the creek, a calm pick after a busy holiday. Trails may close for up to three days after rain, so check OC Parks before you go.

vetPlaybook.title: Emergency visits: what actually drives the bill
vetPlaybook.detail: After hours timing, the triage exam, and diagnostics like bloodwork and imaging drive most of the total, before any treatment or overnight stay. Ask what is urgent tonight, what can wait for your regular vet, and for a written estimate with a low and high range before you approve care.
